problem.text: Let $x$ be a real number selected uniformly at random between $100$ and $200$. If $\lfloor \sqrt{x} \rfloor = 12$, find the probability that $\lfloor \sqrt{100x} \rfloor = 120$. ($\lfloor v \rfloor$ means the greatest integer less than or equal to $v$.)

steps.title: Where to start: turn each floor condition into an interval
steps.body: Because $x$ is chosen uniformly, probabilities are ratios of lengths. So translate each floor statement into an interval for $x$. The key fact: $\lfloor v \rfloor = k$ means exactly $k \le v < k + 1$.

your_turn.prompt: What interval of $x$ does $\lfloor \sqrt{x} \rfloor = 12$ give, and how long is it?
your_turn.answer: $12 \le \sqrt{x} < 13$, so $144 \le x < 169$, an interval of length $25$ (it lies inside $100$ to $200$).

steps.title: Translate the second condition
steps.body: In the same way, $\lfloor \sqrt{100x} \rfloor = 120$ means $120 \le \sqrt{100x} < 121$. Squaring gives $14400 \le 100x < 14641$, so $144 \le x < 146.41$. Careful: $\sqrt{100x} = 10\sqrt{x}$, but $\lfloor 10\sqrt{x} \rfloor$ is not the same as $10\lfloor \sqrt{x} \rfloor$.

your_turn.answer: For example $x = 150$: $\sqrt{15000} \approx 122.5$, so the floor is $122$.

steps.title: Set up the conditional probability
steps.body: We are told that $\lfloor \sqrt{x} \rfloor = 12$, so $x$ is uniform on $144 \le x < 169$. The probability is the length of the part of that interval where the second condition also holds, divided by the length of the whole interval.

your_turn.prompt: Why do we divide by $25$ and not by $100$ (the length from $100$ to $200$)?
your_turn.answer: The condition $\lfloor \sqrt{x} \rfloor = 12$ is given, so only $x$ in $[144, 169)$ are still possible.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
The interval $144 \le x < 146.41$ lies entirely inside $144 \le x < 169$, and its length is $2.41$. So the probability is
$$\frac{2.41}{25} = \frac{241}{2500}.$$
The answer is **(B)**.

wrong_choices.C: This comes from treating $\sqrt{x}$ as uniform on $[12, 13)$ and asking for $\sqrt{x} < 12.1$. But $x$ is the uniform quantity, not $\sqrt{x}$, so you must compare lengths of $x$-intervals.
wrong_choices.E: This comes from assuming $\lfloor \sqrt{100x} \rfloor = 10\lfloor \sqrt{x} \rfloor$. That is false: at $x = 150$ the left side is $122$, not $120$.
